resources.string: Turn on a backup of your history?
Keep with my contacts
Not now

A backup brings your conversations back on a new phone by your 24 words; it is sealed with them, and nobody else can open it. The people you write to keep it: each keeps a sealed part and sees only its size. Montana\'s nodes only pass messages on and keep no copy. This phone also keeps sealed parts for your contacts, up to 1 GB, and cannot open them. This is asked once; both are in Settings → Data and Storage.

This way your copy lives only on phones: Montana\'s nodes keep none of it. It is sealed with your 24 words and cut into parts, and the people you write to keep the parts for you: each sees only a size, never a word. On a new phone your 24 words bring the parts back, and your conversations with them.

The parts your contacts leave with you are sealed the same way: this phone cannot open them, and only their own 24 words can. This is how Montana keeps copies with no cloud in between: people hold each other\'s sealed parts, and no one but the owner can ever read them.
